rationale: C12 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child's second operative provision. Both are short amendatory executive orders using the distinctive machinery of changing specified institutional terminology wherever it occurs in an earlier order and its title. C04 and C13 also use closely related amendment forms, but C12 most nearly matches the child's wording and scope.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The words "Secretary of the Army" are substituted for the words "Secretary of War" wherever the latter words occur in such order or in the title thereof.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The words "Air Force," are inserted after the word "Army," wherever such word occurs in the said order and in the title thereof.
shared_material.explanation: Both provisions globally revise specified terminology throughout a prior order and its title, using nearly identical sentence structure and administrative machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Section 4 of such order is amended by adding thereto at the end thereof the following paragraph
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Part I A 1, General, of the said order is amended to provide that...
shared_material.explanation: Both directives are organized as numbered amendments that identify a precise portion of an earlier order and state the replacement or addition directly.
